sub_scenario.one_line: architectural acoustician: the wing first, for the treated room

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the calibration files and closing stale entries.
The measurement rig review wrapped early today.
Client meetings and site surveys, chaotic by nature, are enjoyable parts of the job.
Someone new shadowed me in the listening room this morning.
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the model validations into one message before lunch.
My simulation calibrations are accurate because they happen in the treated listening room; the two flagship projects this year validated within one decibel, both calibrated there.
The treated room is the accuracy mechanism.
Report writing happens anywhere; words are noise-proof in a way calibrations are not.
I archived last cycle's notes on the measurement rig and set up the new folder.
As fresh as these things get.
Ironically, acoustic calibration is the one task in this firm that cannot survive bad acoustics.
The task defines its own seating requirement.
A vendor call about the calibration files ran long but ended well.
I walked through the listening room checklist with the new starter.
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the model validations.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the measurement rig records and fixed it at the source.

The seat reshuffle offers two options: the listening-room wing with booking priority, or the open atrium desks; my one atrium-calibrated project validated three decibels out and needed a costly re-measure.
One atrium calibration, one costly re-measure.
The only re-measure of my career.
I sketched next week's plan for the model validations before leaving.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the calibration files updates.
Both seat options carry the same desk allowance and the same commute.
I compared two options for the measurement rig tooling and noted a mild preference.
I closed the week by updating the listening room handover notes.
Seat preferences are due Friday: the listening-room wing or the atrium desks first on my form?
